description: The CipherScribe nib and suggestions panel. Both are non-activating overlays driven entirely from Rust (show/hide/move are commands, not JS window calls), so core:default covers them - see capabilities/search.json for why an omitted window fails silently. allow-listen/allow-emit are named explicitly because both are load-bearing and both fail silently: the windows RENDER from the nib_state/panel_data events they listen for, and the panel's 'Turn off for <exe>' hands the write to the main window by emitting scribe-disable-app (settings are a per-webview cache, so the panel must not write them itself).
